text:
maya: Heads-up — onboarding orion-v2-int8; multilang detok smoke failed for a small but reproducible subset: CJK + mixed ASCII/fullwidth quotes.
ashwin: can you paste a minimal repro?
maya: minimal input: "他说: \"Hello\" 她说: ‘你好’". Expected detok preserves both fullwidth and ASCII quotes in place. On int8 build we see the left fullwidth quote dropped on the first clause.
liwei: is this at tokenization time or detokenization?
maya: detok — token ids look fine pre-emit, but streaming chunks show a one-token shift after the ASCII quote. fp16 baseline (orion-v2-fp16) is clean.
tereza: interesting. which kernel path + hardware?
maya: a100, sm90 optimized int8 path (q8-fast-kernel). Repro steps I ran: 
```
python -m evals.run --model orion-v2-int8 --suite cjk-detok --case "quotes-mix" --dump-token-ids --streaming
```
attach output snippet:
```
INPUT: 他说: "Hello" 她说: ‘你好’
TOK_IDS_PRE: [3452, 58, 101, 204, 4567, ...]
STREAM_CHUNK_1: [3452, 58, 101, 204]
STREAM_CHUNK_2: [4567, ...]
DETOK_CHUNK_1: 他说: "Hello
DETOK_CHUNK_2: 她说: ‘你好’
OBSERVED: missing leading fullwidth quote before 他说 in final detok (quote dropped between chunks)
```
ashwin: so chunk boundary seems to lose a prefix char when it crosses ascii->fullwidth transition. Could be KV cache offset + subtoken boundary.
liwei: can you run same case with --force-no-streaming to see if non-streaming output matches?
maya: good idea — non-streaming output is correct. That points to streaming assembly.
tereza: maybe the streaming assembly code assumes byte-length continuity and our tokenizer split uses multi-byte UTF-8 boundaries; kernel emits token count but chunk byte offsets are different in quant path.
maya: also saw a small BLEU delta in automated runs: deploy-bot: eval job 2623456792 finished — cjk-detok/quotes-mix: BLEU -1.28 vs fp16 (p<0.01).
ashwin: can you attach the --dump-token-ids for both streaming chunks and the full non-streaming run? Also include raw bytes around the quote characters (hex).
maya: pasted hex around boundary: 
```
... e4 bd a0 e5 a5 bd 22 20 e5 a5 b3 ...
```
(22 is ASCII 0x22, fullwidth quote is multi-byte sequence)
liwei: confirming — looks like when the kernel writes chunk boundary it reports token count but not byte-length; assembler slices byte ranges based on token->byte mapping from fp16 path; mismatch in q8 kernel mapping leads to drop.
tereza: hypothesis: quant kernel uses an alternate subtoken packing for common ASCII punctuation to squeeze tokens, changing byte positions. Need a reproducer that toggles kernel flags.
maya: quick test flags: q8-kernel=fast vs q8-kernel=safe. fast reproduces bug, safe matches fp16.
ashwin: great, that narrows it. Can someone open a small PR to add an assertion in streaming assembler that validates token->byte mapping per-chunk in debug mode? If mismatch abort and fall back to slow path.
liwei: I'll take the PR. Also will add a unit test with mixed ascii/fullwidth punctuation and a streaming chunk boundary at that spot.
maya: filed issue #987 (link: https://redwood/issue/987) with logs and attached dumps.
tereza: for release notes — mark as regression for orion-v2-int8 on sm90 fast-kernel; workaround: set q8-kernel=safe or disable streaming for critical CJK locales.
maya: thanks y'all — assigning to @liwei for PR, @ashwin can you triage whether to gate the fast kernel behind a rollout flag?
ashwin: yes, will discuss with runtime team. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: job 2623456796 started: run cjk-detok smoke with q8-kernel=safe
maya: follow-ups: add a short perf test (latency delta) for safe vs fast to quantify impact before gating.
liwei: on it, will post numbers in the thread.
